title: Appian occupies both the orchestration and the app-layer slot, making it displacement rather than integration
content:
Appian is recorded as not a complement. It is proprietary low-code process automation that occupies the same slot as Camunda and the application layer as well, so the conclusion is displacement, not addition.

This is worth stating separately from the Mendix and OutSystems calls because the reasoning is doubled. Against a pure low-code app platform the collision is at the app layer; against a pure BPMN engine there is a documented seam where the record layer attaches. Appian closes both, which removes the fallback argument that works for Camunda partners.

Two leads carry this finding, both from the provisional v2 ranking tail: NextWave Consulting in the UK at "2 · decide thesis first" and Valcon in NL at "9 · do not pitch". Both source rows record long-standing Appian practices, and Valcon's also records roughly ten years of Mendix work — so this lead sits inside two displacement groups at once, which is consistent with its do-not-pitch marking.
